learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of building complete thoughts and learn how to identify the four superpower types of sentences in English grammar!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense when put together. For example, 'The cat is sleeping' is a complete sentence, but 'in the park' is just a phrase because it does not give us the full story!

main_concepts.concept_title: 👤 The Star and The Action: Subject & Predicate
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every complete sentence has two main parts. The Subject is the star of the sentence (who or what we are talking about), and the Predicate is the action part that tells us what the star is doing!
These are the most common sentences that simply state a fact, share an idea, or tell us some information. They always end with a neat little full stop, like 'I love eating chocolate ice cream.'

Whenever you want to know something or gather information, you use an interrogative sentence! These sentences ask a direct question and always end with a curvy question mark, like 'Where did you hide my favorite comic book?'
These sentences give a command, make a gentle request, or offer advice. They usually end with a full stop, like 'Please pass the salt' or the bossier 'Clean your room right now!'

When you are super excited, totally surprised, or even scared, you use an exclamatory sentence! These express sudden, strong feelings and end with an exclamation mark, like 'What a beautifully painted rainbow that is!'

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Super Sentence Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Think about your absolute favorite video game, movie, or pet. Write down exactly four sentences about it: one Declarative, one Interrogative, one Imperative, and one Exclamatory!

quick_recap: ⭐ A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense, containing both a Subject and a Predicate.
⭐ There are four main kinds of sentences: Declarative (tells), Interrogative (asks), Imperative (commands or requests), and Exclamatory (expresses strong emotion).
